title: The Tide of Maple Hollow
premise: Marisol Fairweather keeps her grandfather's lighthouse and her heart locked tight, writing romance novels under a pen name while refusing to live one. When a clerical error names her and Callum Reyes—her late brother's best friend and the town's disgraced former deputy—as co-owners of the Hollow Orchard, the two are legally bound to settle the deed within ninety days or lose the land to a developer with a judge in his pocket. Forced into partnership, they uncover that Marisol's grandfather forged the original transfer to protect Callum from an unjust conviction years ago. As their guarded alliance deepens into love, they must expose the real culprit at a public hearing, forgive themselves for old silences, and choose each other openly; the book ends with the orchard saved, the deed rewritten in both their names by choice, and Marisol publishing her first novel under her own name.
about_author: Astrid Dunmore is the pen name of a former small-town archivist who spent a decade cataloguing deeds, diaries, and unsent letters along the Atlantic coast. She writes romances about people who mistake duty for destiny, and she still cannot walk past an abandoned orchard without inventing a story.

chapters.title: The Keeper's Arithmetic
chapters.summary: Marisol's POV. She maintains the lighthouse, drafts her novel in secret, and recites her creed that hearts can be trained like muscles. A letter arrives naming her co-owner of the orchard she thought belonged solely to her family. Emotional beat: controlled solitude cracked open by paperwork.

chapters.title: Two Names on One Deed
chapters.summary: Callum's POV. He reads the same letter in his rented room above the hardware store, recognizing Marisol's name and dreading hers. The developer, Ambrose Pell, has already made him an offer. Emotional beat: dread sharpening into resolve—he won't be run out twice.

chapters.title: Ninety Days
chapters.summary: Dual POV. The estranged pair meet at the county records office and learn the deadline: settle or sell within ninety days. Their first argument in eight years happens over a photocopier. Emotional beat: hostile electricity neither will name.

chapters.title: The Orchard Remembers
chapters.summary: Marisol's POV. Walking the overgrown rows, she finds her grandfather's grafting marks and a hidden strongbox key reference. Callum arrives uninvited; they work in prickly silence and almost talk. Emotional beat: grief surfacing through soil and memory.

chapters.title: What the Town Says
chapters.summary: Callum's POV. At the diner, old neighbors still whisper about his resignation after the warehouse fire conviction he didn't commit. Marisol defends him before she can stop herself. Emotional beat: shame met, unexpectedly, by loyalty.

chapters.title: Pell's Paper Trail
chapters.summary: Marisol's POV. She discovers Pell's option contract predates the deed error—he engineered the whole crisis. She tells Callum; they agree to a temporary truce. Emotional beat: suspicion redirected toward a common enemy.

chapters.title: Grafts and Grief
chapters.summary: Callum's POV. He teaches Marisol winter pruning as they prepare the orchard against frost, and finally mentions her brother Danny's last night alive. Marisol walks out. Emotional beat: the wound beneath the wound exposed.

chapters.title: The Strongbox
chapters.summary: Marisol's POV. In the lighthouse cellar she opens her grandfather's strongbox: the original deed transfer, forged, dated three days after the fire—a deliberate act to shield Callum. Emotional beat: betrayal and devotion tangled in one signature.

chapters.title: Confessions at Low Tide
chapters.summary: Callum's POV. Confronted, Callum admits he knew nothing of the forgery but confesses why he never fought the conviction: protecting Danny's reputation. Marisol realizes her silence hurt them both. Emotional beat: mutual guilt laid bare on the tideline.

chapters.title: A Chapter Written Backwards
chapters.summary: Marisol's POV. Stuck on her novel, she realizes every hero she's written is a man who stays—and she's been writing apologies to Callum for years. She deletes her safe ending. Emotional beat: art as confession.

chapters.title: Frost Warning
chapters.summary: Dual POV. An early freeze threatens the blossom crop; they work through the night running smudge pots, laughing for the first time. Pell watches from the road. Emotional beat: warmth kindled in shared labor, witnessed by threat.

chapters.title: The Deputy's File
chapters.summary: Callum's POV. He retrieves his old case file from a sympathetic retired clerk: the fire marshal's report was altered, and the alteration traces to Pell's uncle, then a county official. Emotional beat: hope arriving disguised as evidence.

chapters.title: Witness
chapters.summary: Marisol's POV. They track down the retired fire marshal living in a coastal cabin; he agrees to testify but warns that Pell's judge friend controls the hearing calendar. Emotional beat: fragile courage, borrowed time.

chapters.title: Almost
chapters.summary: Callum's POV. After the cabin trip, rain strands them overnight; almost-kiss, interrupted by Marisol's own retreat—she quotes her heart-as-muscle creed aloud and hates how it sounds. Emotional beat: desire colliding with self-protection.

chapters.title: Pell Makes His Move
chapters.summary: Marisol's POV. Pell offers Marisol full ownership if she sells out Callum's claim, revealing he knows about the forgery and will press charges otherwise. Emotional beat: temptation framed as mercy, refused at cost.

chapters.title: The Mirror
chapters.summary: Callum's POV. Marisol confesses Pell's offer; instead of anger, Callum sees his own years of cowardice reflected in her bargain. They fight honestly, then hold on. Emotional beat: forgiveness of the person in the mirror begins.

chapters.title: Deadline Week
chapters.summary: Dual POV. With days left, the hearing is scheduled—before the deed deadline, deliberately. Evidence goes missing from the clerk's office; the retired marshal's testimony is now their only card. Emotional beat: cornered but united.

chapters.title: The Hearing
chapters.summary: Marisol's POV. Before a packed courthouse, the marshal testifies; Pell's lawyer discredits him until Marisol produces her grandfather's sealed letter, written to be opened 'when the truth needs a witness.' Emotional beat: the dead speaking, the room turning.

chapters.title: What Justice Costs
chapters.summary: Callum's POV. The judge, cornered by publicity and the letter, vacates the conviction and voids Pell's option—but the forgery charge looms unless someone claims responsibility. Marisol stands and claims it as her grandfather's act, accepting liability. Emotional beat: justice purchased with personal risk.

chapters.title: Ninety Days, Last One
chapters.summary: Dual POV. On the final day, with the land legally theirs jointly, they could partition and part ways forever. Instead, at the orchard gate, Callum asks her to stay not because of a deed. She says yes. Emotional beat: choice replacing obligation.

chapters.title: Blossom Tide
chapters.summary: Marisol's POV. Spring bloom over Maple Hollow; the town that whispered now celebrates. Marisol signs a publishing contract under her real name, dedicating the novel to 'the man who stayed.' Emotional beat: visibility chosen, belonging earned.

chapters.title: The Light We Keep
chapters.summary: Epilogue, alternating POVs. One year later: the orchard thriving, Callum deputized again by a reformed department, Marisol reading her opening chapter aloud at the harvest festival. The lighthouse beam sweeps the rows. Emotional beat: love and duty reconciled—the tide comes in, and this time they let it.
